app.title: CPRD Extractor
app.summary: A researcher builds a clinical code list by matching candidate SNOMED CT and ICD-10 codes against the practice dictionary, or picks conditions and drugs from built-in libraries. They can narrow the run to patients from an earlier extraction or to an uploaded list of IDs, then extract the matching records from every practice folder while a progress bar tracks the scan. Next they assemble a cohort: they load a starting population and apply inclusion criteria one at a time, such as age, sex, registration period, a diagnosis, a drug, a hospital record or linkage eligibility. A funnel chart shows how many patients remain after each step. They end with a cohort file or record extract in Parquet or CSV, with code descriptions added, ready for analysis.

task.text: Turn clinical code lists into extracted patient records and a filtered study cohort, with a count of the patients left after each criterion.

data.text: Electronic health record tables: coded primary-care observations and prescriptions, linked hospital and death records, patient demographics, and dictionaries that map clinical codes to the database's internal codes.
data.item: a coded clinical record for one patient (an observation, a drug issue, or a hospital episode)

stage.text: extracting records and assembling a study cohort from health records, before analysis

mechanism.text: Pages in a sidebar each carry one stage of the work and hand their output to the next. Matched codes from the code-list pipeline or the drug lookup are pushed into the extraction tabs, and a patient scope chosen on one page limits later extractions. The cohort builder applies one filter at a time and redraws an attrition funnel. Each result table offers CSV or Parquet download and is also saved to disk.

field.text: code-list-based cohort extraction from electronic health records in epidemiology

workflow.name: build a filtered cohort from coded records and export it

steps.here: A Data Mode radio picks mock data, a cluster, a custom server path or a Windows folder; the CPRD root is set and the folder structure is detected

steps.step: define the set of codes that identifies the condition
steps.here: Stage 5 parses pasted or uploaded SNOMED CT and ICD-10 codes and matches them to medcodeids in the EMIS dictionary, with tabs for matched, unmatched, expansion and audit log. Stage 6 exports an Excel workbook for a clinician to mark Include, Exclude or Uncertain; the drug lookup turns drug names, brand names and BNF codes into product codes

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Patient scope limits an extraction to all patients, the patients from the previous extraction, or a pasted or uploaded list of IDs

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Choose codes from the disease or drug library, type them in, upload them or accept codes pushed from another page, then run the extraction. It scans every practice folder in parallel while a progress tracker shows the scan, and reports how many records and unique patients it found

steps.step: apply inclusion criteria one at a time
steps.here: Load a starting population, then add one criterion after another (age range at a reference year, sex, registration window, has a SNOMED diagnosis, has a drug, has a HES ICD-10 record, linkage eligible). Each criterion narrows the patients left by the one before

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: A funnel chart shows the patient count after each criterion as a share of the starting population, and the sidebar shows the records and patients in the last extraction
Download CSV or Parquet, optionally with readable column names and code descriptions added. Every extraction and the final cohort are also saved to the output folder

distinctive: Codes cross between coding systems: SNOMED CT is mapped to the database's own medcodeids through a dictionary, ICD-10 is used for hospital and death records, and BNF codes for drugs
The code list is checked by a clinician outside the tool: it generates an Include, Exclude or Uncertain workbook with an audit trail
An attrition funnel records how many patients each inclusion criterion removes, as cohort reporting requires
Linkage eligibility decides which patients can appear in hospital and death data, so it is one of the cohort filters
The same extraction can be run as batch jobs on an HPC cluster, using generated Slurm job-array scripts and a merge step

parts.title: Sidebar: data mode, output settings and navigation
parts.summary: Chooses the data environment and output format, moves between modules, and shows the record and patient counts of the last extraction.

parts.title: Code List Development
parts.summary: Six tabbed stages. In the two working stages, candidate codes are matched against the practice dictionary and a clinician review workbook is exported.

parts.title: Drug Lookup
parts.summary: Searches a curated drug library by BNF code, name or therapeutic class against the product dictionary, collects the matching product codes and pushes them to drug extraction.

parts.title: CPRD Aurum Extraction
parts.summary: Tabs for extracting by medcode, by SNOMED code, by drug, or a whole file type. Codes come from the libraries, a paste, an upload or another page, and every practice folder is scanned with progress shown.

parts.title: Patient scope selector
parts.summary: Limits an extraction to all patients, to the patients in the previous extraction, or to a custom list of IDs.

parts.title: Results table and export
parts.summary: Previews the extracted records, gives a plain-language summary, and saves the result as CSV or Parquet with readable column names and code descriptions.

parts.title: Cohort Builder
parts.summary: Loads a starting population and applies inclusion criteria one after another, each narrowing the patients left by the one before, then exports the final cohort.
